A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TIIF-Bench and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across extensive revision, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-model benchmark results, human-preference correlations, qualitative evaluations, and appendix experiments using GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-VL-72B.

after.justification: v3 reports benchmark results, evaluator-training ablations, human-labeled evaluator validation, and a new text-rendering metric preference study.

M1.justification: v1 uses off-the-shelf GPT-4o or Qwen2.5-VL-72B for checklist evaluation. v3 introduces a trained Qwen3VL-8B TIIF-Evaluator that generates reasoning before binary answers, and replaces yes/no style assessment with aspect-ratio-matched reference-image similarities. Prompt composition and the GNED formula remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The original 5,000 English prompts and evaluation dimensions are retained, but v3 introduces an evaluator-training corpus of generated images and annotated binary questions, whereas v1 performs no evaluator training. It also adds style-reference image sets and extends empirical prompt-diversity analysis to additional benchmark corpora, including Gecko, WISE, and LongT2I-Bench.

E2.justification: The main comparison adds Qwen-Image, FLUX.2 Dev, BAGEL, Emu3.5 variants, and Nano-Banana variants, while removing several earlier rows, including Playground, LlamaGen, and LightGen. In the corresponding GenAI Bench and CompBench++ comparisons, Nano-Banana replaces FLUX.1 Pro and MidJourney v7 replaces the reported v6/v6.1 comparator. Evaluator validation also introduces comparisons against off-the-shelf Qwen3VL-8B.

E3.justification: v3 changes benchmark scoring through its trained evaluator and reference-based style metric. New experimental protocols include a balanced 560-question held-out validation set, one-epoch training for three evaluator paradigms, a 100-case text-metric preference study using identical OCR outputs, and per-generator AUROC validation. The earlier ten-participant, three-sets-per-dimension ranking protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds evaluator-training ablations, human-label validation across eight generators, and a controlled comparison of GNED, PNED, and OCR Recall. It expands semantic-redundancy analysis but removes the earlier t-SNE analysis, GPT-4o/Qwen2.5 ranking-agreement analysis, and explicit full-benchmark versus testmini consistency checks.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies two generation rollouts per model over all 5,000 prompts when constructing the evaluator corpus. This is repetition information for new data collection, not evidence that the earlier benchmark experiments received additional repeated runs. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The main leaderboard contains extensively revised entries and rankings, including NB-Pro scores of 93.1/93.3 in v3 Table 2. New findings include 91.07% reasoning-evaluator accuracy and 83%/94%/99% human-preference agreement for Recall/PNED/GNED. Earlier full-set and Qwen-scored tables disappear, while the human Spearman correlations are retained. Changed scoring prevents interpreting leaderboard differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The binary-match scoring equation and GNED definition, normalization, and bounds are unchanged. v3 Figure 6 adds a concrete counterexample to PNED's length comparability: duplicating the target and omission pattern changes PNED from 1 to 2 while GNED remains 0.5. No new theorem or general proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 makes a dedicated, reproducible evaluator with interpretable reasoning a central contribution, extending v1's claim of a fine-grained VLM questioning framework. Reference-image-based style assessment also becomes an explicit contribution in the abstract and conclusion. The hierarchical benchmark and GNED contributions are retained.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes consistent rankings from two off-the-shelf evaluators; v3 instead develops an argument for task-specific adaptation using Qwen3VL-8B verification tests. It justifies choosing reasoning over the slightly more accurate classifier for interpretability and explains how aspect-ratio matching should reduce layout-related style mismatches. The stated limitations concerning English, common objects, and linguistic register remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents the evaluator backbone, balanced 218K-question training set, annotation process, one-epoch training, revised evaluation prompt, reference-image sources, aspect ratios, and checklist statistics. v1's project-page pointer is omitted. However, style aggregation is inconsistent: Section 3.3 averages CSD and DINOv3, whereas Appendix A4.2 additionally includes SigLIP2.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands discussion of question-based evaluation, newer reward models, long-prompt benchmarks, and reasoning benchmarks. It distinguishes unified models from autoregressive generators and positions TIIF-Evaluator against closed-API evaluation and unadapted general-purpose VLMs. These are substantive positioning changes beyond reference updates.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, evaluation discussion, and model analyses undergo extensive rewriting. The separate user-study section is merged into Section 4.2, appendices are reorganized around statistics, prompts, experiments, and visualizations, and references move after the appendices. Model terminology and author information also change.

P2.justification: The original multi-panel diversity figure is replaced by an expanded benchmark comparison, and the construction pipeline is redrawn. v3 adds PNED and AUROC figures plus statistics and text-metric tables, removes several earlier results tables, and relocates the concept-pool table and human-study illustration. Typography, page layout, and numerous captions also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The new human-labeled evaluator validation and controlled text-metric study strengthen evidence beyond v1's ranking correlations and qualitative examples. However, v3 removes full-set and cross-evaluator checks while introducing conflicting style-score definitions and unexplained discrepancies between the Text scores in Table 2 and GNED values in Table A3. Because these issues affect core evaluation reliability and reproducibility, the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
